question: Convert 3 radians to degrees.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that 1 radian ≈ 57.2958°.

To convert radians to degrees directly, multiply the given value by 57.2958.

⇒ 3 radians = 3 × 57.2958°

⇒ 3 radians = 171.8874°

Rounding to two decimal places gives 171.89°.

**∴ The correct answer is 171.89°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle = 3 radians

**Formula Used:**

Angle in Degrees = Angle in Radians × (180 ÷ π)

 

 

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 
 3 radians
 π rad
 ∴ 3 radians ≈ 171.89°
 0°
 180°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Degrees = 3 × (180 ÷ π)

⇒ Degrees = 540 ÷ π

⇒ Degrees = 540 ÷ 3.14159

⇒ Degrees ≈ 171.8874°

⇒ Degrees ≈ 171.89°

**∴ The correct answer is 171.89°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Degree to Radian Conversion

To convert an angle from degrees to radians, multiply the value by (π ÷ 180). For example, 90° = 90 × (π ÷ 180) = π ÷ 2 radians.

Definition of a Radian

One radian is the angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius of the circle.

Common Standard Angles

Some frequently used conversions are: 30° = π ÷ 6, 45° = π ÷ 4, 60° = π ÷ 3, and 180° = π radians.
